title: Invariance of the coarse conditioning under flipping Alice's special bit
statement: Fix $n \ge 1$, and let $\omega$ be a sample of the hard distribution: a special coordinate $T \in \{0,1,\dots,n-1\}$, bits $x_T$ and $y_T$ for Alice and Bob at that coordinate, and a disjointness type assigned to every coordinate. From $\omega$ form the coarse conditioning $(T,\, X_{<T},\, Y_{>T})$, where $X_{<T}$ is Alice's input bits at the coordinates strictly below $T$ (padded with $\mathrm{false}$ elsewhere) and $Y_{>T}$ is Bob's input bits at the coordinates strictly above $T$ (padded with $\mathrm{false}$ elsewhere). Let $\omega'$ be obtained from $\omega$ by toggling only Alice's special bit $x_T$, leaving $T$, $y_T$, and all coordinate types unchanged. Then $\omega$ and $\omega'$ produce the same coarse conditioning: $(T,\, X_{<T},\, Y_{>T})$ is identical for $\omega'$ and $\omega$.
hypotheses_covered: n is a positive natural number
omega is a hard-distribution sample (special coordinate T, bits x_T and y_T, and a disjointness type at every coordinate)
omega' is omega with only Alice's special bit x_T flipped
